advisory.finding: No test exercises the under-lock rebase-guard / lock-timeout recovery path added by the change: the script calls lock.check_no_rebase_in_progress(tracker) and catches (StoreIncompatibleError, LockTimeout, RebaseGuard) to route to warn() (preserve HEAD). The under-lock tests cover corrupt-epoch, dirty-worktree, and HEAD-change rechecks but never a rebase-in-progress / lock-timeout state, so a regression that let one of those exceptions escape (crashing the `set -eu` ensure script with a non-zero exit and aborting convergence) would go undetected.

evidence: ABSENCE: no test in test_reviewbot_convergence_matrix.py or test_reviewbot_convergence_happy_path.py drives the reset --hard step to a non-zero return while all earlier preconditions pass; the existing git-shim tests intercept diff/rev-parse to abort before reset, never the reset itself
advisory.finding: The `reset --hard` adoption-failure branch introduced by the change (warns 'could not adopt pinned remote commit' when the reset returns non-zero) has no test. The happy-path test covers a successful reset; the under-lock tests all short-circuit before the reset. A regression that mishandled a failed adoption reset (e.g. still printing the 'adopted' success line, or moving HEAD partially) would not be caught.
